What slows logistics teams down

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

  • Tracking data that nobody is watching

    Milestones sit in the TMS, carrier portals, GPS dashboards and WMS screens, but no one compares them with what was promised. Delays, stuck consignments and missed cut-offs surface when the customer calls, and the same lanes, hubs and carriers keep failing without evidence to fix them.

  • Failed deliveries that become returns

    Consignees are unreachable, addresses lack landmarks and some attempts are recorded without a real visit. Re-attempt instructions arrive after the rider has left, and shipments that could have been delivered come back as return-to-origin costs for the merchant and the network.

  • Paper that slows billing and clearance

    Physical PODs, LR copies, invoices and customs documents travel by hand. Billing waits for PODs, clearance waits for a missing certificate or a corrected invoice, and detention and demurrage build up while teams chase paperwork.

  • Documents and permits that expire unnoticed

    Driver licenses, permits, fitness certificates, PUC certificates, insurance and e-way bills all have expiry dates. When they live in folders and WhatsApp photos, a lapse is found at a checkpoint, in an accident claim or during a client audit.

  • Cash and charges that do not reconcile

    COD collections pass through riders, branches, banks and UPI. Trip advances, fuel and tolls are claimed on paper. Storage and handling charges are assembled at month-end. Reconciliation runs on spreadsheets and differences are found weeks later.

  • Compliance built into every movement

    GST e-way bill rules, Motor Vehicles Act documents, customs filing timelines, carrier registration, messaging consent and the DPDP Act all shape how bookings, trips, updates and consignee data may be automated. A shortcut in one workflow can create risk in another.

Shipment exception desk: proactive delay, NDR and SLA alerts

One connected workflow that watches every shipment against what was promised, from pickup to proof of delivery. Milestones from your TMS, carrier feeds, GPS and WMS are compared with SLAs, exceptions get an owner and a deadline, consignees and shippers hear about delays and failed attempts before they call, and their choices flow back into the next dispatch plan.

What changes

  • Customers hear about delays and failed attempts from you before they call
  • Fewer deliverable shipments turned into returns to origin
  • Every exception has a named owner, a deadline and a recorded resolution
  • Reason-coded data that shows which lanes, hubs and carriers need fixing
  1. 1

    Unify every milestone

    Booking, pickup, hub, line-haul, customs, out-for-delivery and delivery events from the TMS, courier and carrier APIs, GPS platforms and the WMS flow into one shipment timeline with the promised date and contract SLA.

    nn8nSSupabase
  2. 2

    Detect exceptions early

    Rules tuned per lane, service and customer flag missed pickups, no-movement, stuck-at-hub, ETA slippage, vessel rollovers, missed warehouse cut-offs and failed delivery attempts, with reason codes from the source system.

    PPythonSSupabase
  3. 3

    Give each exception an owner

    Each exception lands in the control-tower queue with an owner, a deadline and a suggested next step. Owners are alerted in Slack, and cases still open as the SLA limit approaches escalate to the branch or operations head.

    RRetoolSSlack
  4. 4

    Tell the customer first

    Consignees and shippers who opted in get an approved WhatsApp template with the revised ETA or the failed-delivery reason and choices: re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or pickup point. Others get the same choices by DLT-registered SMS.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8n
  5. 5

    Act on the reply

    Button replies are written back to the TMS before the next dispatch plan. An AI model classifies free-text replies, and unclear or disputed ones go to an agent with the shipment history attached.

    OOpenAInn8n
  6. 6

    Close the loop and learn

    PODs, resolution codes and SLA outcomes feed a dashboard by lane, hub, carrier, merchant and client, so the weekly review fixes recurring causes instead of answering individual complaints.

    ddbtMPMicrosoft Power BI

  7. People decide

    Control-tower executives own every exception and approve messages to key accounts, NDR agents handle unclear or disputed replies, hub supervisors review questionable attempts, and merchants approve returns and out-of-rule address changes. No automated message promises compensation or an unconfirmed delivery time.

Start where the work repeats

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

  • Enquiry & quoteFreight RFQ-to-quote with rate cards and margin approvalRead spot and contract rate requests from email, WhatsApp and tender portals, structure them, price each lane from your own buy rates, surcharges and validity dates, and give the pricing lead a draft quote to approve before it reaches the shipper.5–8 weeks
  • Booking & pickup requestBooking and pickup scheduling on WhatsApp and the portalLet merchants book pickups through a WhatsApp Flow, the portal or an API, check serviceability, restricted items and weight before accepting, assign a pickup slot by branch cut-off, and confirm with the AWB, labels and a reminder.4–6 weeks
  • Vehicle & driver assignmentDriver and rider onboarding with document expiry alertsCollect and verify driver and rider documents at onboarding, track every expiry date for licenses, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness and permits, and stop a vehicle or driver with a lapsed document from being assigned.4–6 weeks
  • Vehicle & driver assignmentPreventive maintenance and tire reminders from odometer dataUse GPS odometer readings and service history to schedule preventive maintenance, tire rotation and inspections for each vehicle, warn dispatch before a due vehicle is assigned, and track work orders to closure.3–5 weeks
  • Pickup, receipt & origin handlingInbound ASN-to-GRN tracking with discrepancy alertsMatch each client's advance shipping notice with the vehicle at the dock and the goods received, flag short, excess and damaged lines with photos, and send the client a GRN summary as soon as receiving closes.4–6 weeks
  • In transit, at hubs & at customsE-way bill validity watch with extension and Part B alertsCompare each active e-way bill's validity with the vehicle's GPS position and ETA, warn the trip owner before expiry, prompt Part B updates when goods change vehicles, and prepare extension details for an authorized user to submit.3–5 weeks

Walk through the shipment journey

A clear delivery rhythm

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 1

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We map how bookings, trips, receipts, documents, exceptions, PODs and settlements actually flow, sit with the booking desk, control tower, hub, warehouse, fleet and billing teams, and pick the workflows where automation helps most. We baseline KPIs from TMS, WMS, GPS and accounting data and identify GST, customs, messaging and personal data boundaries early.

  2. 2

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design each workflow with its triggers, data fields, decision rules, approval points and failure paths, plus the WhatsApp and SMS templates, driver and rider flows and review screens people will use. We agree which actions stay with authorized users, such as e-way bill extensions and customs filings, and how consent is collected for consignee and driver messages.

  3. 3

    2–6 weeks

    Build

    We build integrations, workflows, review screens and dashboards in a test environment using sample or masked data, with logging, alerts and role-based access from the start. Each workflow is demonstrated to its owners with real scenarios from their lanes, hubs and clients as it takes shape.

  4. 4

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    Owners test each workflow against real situations: failed deliveries with disputed reasons, partial receipts, rollovers, expiring e-way bills, short COD deposits and unreadable PODs. We launch with one branch, hub, client, port or lane first, run alongside the current process for a short period, and train approvers and exception handlers.

  5. 5

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    We monitor runs, failures, message delivery and AI accuracy, review KPIs with owners each month, tune rules, thresholds and prompts, and add workflows from the backlog. Changes to rate cards, SLAs, portals or regulations follow the same design, test and approval route as the original build.

First pilot: Exception and NDR pilot for one hub, region or lane

A four to six week pilot that connects tracking events for one hub, region or lane, flags delays and failed deliveries, sends approved consignee updates and NDR choices, and gives the control tower one exception queue. Forwarders can pilot the customs checklist for one port instead, and fleets the document register with e-way bill alerts. We compare results with the baseline and decide together whether to extend.

  • Milestone feed from the TMS or courier platform and GPS for one hub, region or lane
  • Delay, no-movement and failed-delivery rules with owners and deadlines
  • Approved WhatsApp and DLT-registered SMS templates for delay updates and NDR choices
  • Write-back of re-attempt instructions and an exception queue for the control tower
  • KPI comparison with the baseline, followed by a go or no-go review

Know whether it is working

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

On-time delivery against promise
Share of shipments delivered by the date and time promised to the customer or set in the SLA, by lane, service, hub and carrier.
First-attempt delivery rate
Share of shipments out for delivery that are delivered on the first attempt, excluding reschedules the consignee requested in advance.
Return-to-origin rate
Share of shipments in a period returned to the merchant after failed attempts or refusal, by merchant, pin code and reason.
Exception resolution time
Median time from an exception being raised, such as a delay, no-movement or failed attempt, to its recorded resolution, by exception type and owner.
